findings.summary: Synthetic panel split: 13 closest to Neighborhood A, 16 to Neighborhood B, 1 neither.
18 of 30 personas look for a late-night spot at least weekly (11 three or more times); 7 never do.
15 of 30 rated likelihood 4-5 and 8 rated 1-2. All four '1' ratings came from Neighborhood B personas; Neighborhood A had none. Top-two-box was 7/13 in A vs 7/16 in B.
Most expected spend is $5-10 per visit (14), then $10-20 (9); 4 under $5, 3 over $20.

Most common themes (respondents mentioning): quality coffee/food 29, comfortable seating 26, safety and cleanliness 24, fair transparent pricing 22, reliable late hours 20, fast friendly service 15, social vibe 14, Wi-Fi/outlets 13.
quotes: It would need to be clean, safe, and actually open when it says it is. Good coffee or a simple snack, fast service, and prices that are clear upfront would make it worth stopping in after a late shift.
Cheap drinks, free Wi-Fi, outlets, and a safe vibe matter most. If I can study or hang with friends without spending a lot, and it's open late, I'd go.

It would need to feel clean, safe, and calm, with decent coffee or simple food at a fair price. If it seemed welcoming to families and regulars instead of just chasing a trend, I'd be more likely to stop in.
If it were quiet enough to sit and talk without feeling rushed, that would make it appealing.

caveats: Flashpoint synthetic panel: 30 AI-generated personas, not real people. Treat results as directional only.
Panel gender was matched to a US adult split; age, race, education and income were invented by the generator, not sampled from Census data.
Uncalibrated run (calibration_version=uncalibrated); persona answers generated by gpt-5.4-mini.
Neighborhood subgroups are tiny (A n=13, B n=16) and should not be generalised.
Q5 theme counts come from Flashpoint's open-end analysis, which could not be filtered to this run; its base (30) matches this run.
